nurse_note_query: The driver brought a torn home-pressure diary. Three entries from the past week are around 176/102, but the dates on two lines are incomplete and the clinic obtained only one seated reading today after the driver rushed in from the car park. He says the tablets were restarted recently and asks if the lower reading remembered from last year cancels the diary. The nurse records possible sustained elevation but cannot verify the series or use last year's figure as today's pressure.

licence:

consistently > 170 systolic or > 100 diastolic 
(treated or untreated).

nurse_note_query: At follow-up, the driver says his repeated pressures have improved since antihypertensive treatment, yet the dose was changed three weeks ago and he has briefly felt faint when standing at the depot. The referral does not document a completed period of stable control, whether the dizziness impairs driving, or a specialist review of relevant organ damage. A colleague's comment that he looks well is recorded as hearsay rather than clearance.
provisional_source_quotes:

by the driver licensing authority subject to 
annual review, taking into account the nature 
of the driving task and information provided 
by the treating specialist* as to whether the 
following criteria are met:
•	 the person is treated with antihypertensive 
therapy and effective control of 
hypertension is achieved over a 4-week 
follow-up period; and
•	 there are no side effects from the 
medication that will impair safe driving; and
•	 there is no evidence of damage to target

nurse_note_query: During night deliveries the driver sometimes sees a second image beside an oncoming vehicle. Closing either eye removes the doubling, but he was symptom-free during this morning's appointment. A routine chart reading was recorded without noting whether glasses were worn, and no examiner measured the position of the double image relative to straight-ahead vision. The nurse does not treat a normal office conversation as proof that the driving symptom has resolved.
provisional_source_quotes:
AFTD2022-VIS-COM-007: A person is not fit to hold an unconditional 
licence or a conditional licence:
•	 if the person experiences any diplopia 
(other than physiological diplopia) within 
20 degrees from central fixation.

nurse_note_query: The driver reports missing cyclists entering from one side. An old printout says 138 degrees across both eyes, while a recent automated field result carries a low-reliability warning and does not state whether the central area was clear. Neither paper confirms a stable defect or the full testing protocol. The nurse asks for a reliable binocular field assessment before treating either number as a current commercial-driving result.
provisional_source_quotes:
AFTD2022-VIS-COM-004: A person is not fit to hold an unconditional 
licence:
•	 if the person has any visual field defect.

AFTD2022-VIS-COM-005: A conditional licence may be considered 
by the driver licensing authority subject 
to annual review, taking into account the 
nature of the driving task and information 
provided by the treating optometrist or 
ophthalmologist as to whether the following 
criteria are met:
•	 the binocular visual field has an extent of 
at least 140 degrees within 10 degrees 
above and below the horizontal midline; 
and
•	 the person has no significant visual 
field loss (scotoma, hemianopia, 
quadrantanopia) that is likely to impede 
driving performance; and
•	 the visual field loss is static and unlikely to 
progress rapidly.

nurse_note_query: The driver follows face-to-face speech while wearing hearing aids but misses radio calls in a running vehicle. A phone image of an audiogram shows some thresholds, although the ear labels and the 3000 Hz row are cut off. It is unclear whether the aids were in place during testing. The nurse cannot calculate an unaided better-ear average from the photograph and requests the signed audiology record.
provisional_source_quotes:
AFTD2022-HEAR-COM-001: Compliance with the standard should be clinically 
assessed initially. If the initial clinical assessment 
indicates possible hearing loss, the person should 
be referred for audiometry.

AFTD2022-HEAR-COM-002: A person is not fit to hold an unconditional licence:
•	 if the person has unaided hearing loss ≥ 40 dB 
in the better ear (averaged over the frequencies 
0.5, 1, 2 and 3 KHz).

The driver says an earlier workplace screen had passed him, but that screen did not record the frequencies or better-ear calculation. The assessment needs the commercial threshold and any route involving hearing assistance, with the exact boundary preserved rather than rounded.

nurse_note_query: After an unresponsive spell at a loading bay, the driver remembers sitting down but not a coworker calling his name. The witness is unsure whether there were two episodes or one prolonged episode. An ECG has been arranged and a neurology referral remains open; neither clinician has established a mechanism. The nurse records the possibility of transient loss of awareness without assigning it to a cardiac, neurological or metabolic diagnosis.

and referral to several specialists. People should 
be advised not to drive until the mechanism is

nurse_note_query: The driver became faint during a blood draw and recovered quickly after lying down. He calls it a harmless needle reaction, but the nurse has only his account; a separate unwitnessed spell at home is also mentioned in an old referral. The assessment needs to distinguish a clearly provoked faint from an event of uncertain nature before applying a return-to-driving interval.
provisional_source_quotes:
AFTD2022-BLK-COM-002: 1.2.2. Vasovagal syncope5
The most common cause of transient loss of 
consciousness is vasovagal syncope (‘fainting’). 
Where this has been triggered by a well-defined 
provoking factor or a situation that is unlikely 
to recur while driving (e.g. prolonged standing, 
venepuncture or emotional situation), it is not 
necessary to restrict driving. However, vasovagal 
syncope may also result from other causes 
that are not so benign. In such cases, fitness 
to drive should be assessed according to the 
cardiovascular conditions standards for syncope 
(refer to section 2. Cardiovascular conditions).

AFTD2022-BLK-COM-004: A person should not drive for 5 
years following a single blackout of 
undetermined nature.
A person should not drive for 10 years 
following two or more blackouts of 
undetermined nature separated by a 24-
hour period.
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional 
licence:
•	 if the person has experienced blackouts 
that cannot be diagnosed as syncope, 
seizure or another condition.
If there has been a single blackout or more 
than one blackout within a 24-hour period, 
a conditional licence may be considered 
by the driver licensing authority subject to 
at least annual review, taking into account 
information provided by an appropriate 
specialist as to whether the following 
criterion is met:
•	 there have been no further blackouts for 
at least 5 years.

nurse_note_query: The driver used to manage diabetes with food choices alone, but a current prescription list now includes a nightly insulin injection. He has brought a few meter screenshots rather than a continuous monitoring record and cannot remember the last specialist appointment. The nurse separates the current injected treatment from the historical diet-only description and requests the information needed for commercial-driver review.
provisional_source_quotes:
AFTD2022-DM-COM-007: A person is not fit to hold an unconditional 
licence:
•	 if the person has insulin-treated diabetes.

AFTD2022-DM-COM-009: 3.3.2. Recommendation and 
review of conditional licences for 
commercial vehicle drivers
It is a general requirement that conditional 
licences for commercial vehicle drivers are 
issued by the driver licensing authority based on 
advice from an appropriate medical specialist 
(endocrinologist or consultant physician 
specialising in diabetes) and that these drivers 
are reviewed periodically by the specialist to 
determine their ongoing fitness to drive (refer 
to Part A section 4.4. Conditional licences). For 
commercial drivers receiving insulin treatment, at 
least three months of blood glucose monitoring 
records should be reviewed in assessing fitness 
to drive.

nurse_note_query: A driver taking glucose-lowering medication became confused after a missed meal and a coworker gave him a sugary drink because he could not respond to the meter alarm. No glucose reading was captured until after treatment, and there is no clinician's account of the episode. He denies losing consciousness. The nurse records the assistance and uncertainty separately, then asks for assessment of severe hypoglycaemia and the related commercial-driving restrictions.
provisional_source_quotes:
AFTD2022-DM-COM-002: Non-driving period after a ‘severe 
hypoglycaemic event’
If a severe hypoglycaemic event occurs (as 
defined in section 3.2.1. Hypoglycaemia), the 
person should not drive for a significant period 
of time and will need to be urgently assessed. 
The minimum period of time before returning 
to drive is generally six weeks because it often 
takes many weeks for patterns of glucose 
control and behaviour to be re-established and 
for any temporary ‘impaired hypoglycaemia 
awareness’ to resolve (see below). The non-
driving period will depend on factors such 
as identifying the reason for the episode, the 
specialist’s opinion and the type of motor vehicle 
licence. The specialist’s recommendation for 
returning to driving should be based on the 
patient’s behaviour and objective measures of 
glycaemic control (documented blood glucose) 
over a reasonable interval.

AFTD2022-DM-COM-008: A conditional licence may be considered 
by the driver licensing authority subject to at 
least annual review, taking into consideration 
the nature of the driving task and information 
provided by an endocrinologist or consultant 
physician specialising in diabetes on whether 
the following criteria are met:
